thread:
maya: Heads up — we have a spike of GPU pods Pending in apse1-rack-D. Scheduler logs show repeated 'solver OOM' failures and a bunch of tiny preempts.
cheng: Seeing same. NIC egress to our artifact store hit 95% around the time, lots of latebinds piling up.
sam: Quick snapshot: `kubectl get pods -n ml --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide` shows ~60 pods stuck across two nodes, many with nodeAffinity to nvlink-enabled racks.
leo: Any recent label/annotation rollouts on GPU node pools?
nisha: We pushed the `gpu-favor: low` label syncer patch an hour ago, rolled back for a minute earlier but it came back as part of the automated sync.
maya: Scheduler excerpt (fwiw):
```
I0331 12:07:10 solver.go:412] allocation attempt=47: compute placements failed: runtime: out of memory
I0331 12:07:10 solver.go:413] reducedSearchDepth -> retry
I0331 12:07:11 solver.go:417] allocation attempt=48: compute placements succeeded but preempted 18 pods
```
cheng: That exact OOM loop is the searcher trying to respect strict affinity+taints + network egress constraints. Search depth spikes with many tiny pods and the state graph explodes.
sam: Short-term mitigation: lower scheduler search depth and fall back to cheaper heuristic. We can flip `--placement-search-depth=3` to avoid exponential blowups.
leo: Tradeoff is cost — heuristics increase fragmentation but cut solver mem. Need to estimate.
nisha: Also we can throttle warmpool attach egress so nodes aren't blocked waiting on PV/artifact downloads. If nodes free faster, solver state shrinks.
maya: Proposed immediate steps: 1) set search-depth=3 in canary region apse1, 2) pause label-syncer change to gpu-favor, 3) throttle artifact egress for warmpool attaches.
ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-8352, severity=high — assigned to eng-platform.
sam: Applying search-depth canary now to apse1-rack-D subset (2 schedulers). Patch command: `kubectl patch deployment scheduler -n infra --patch '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"kube-scheduler","args":["--placement-search-depth=3"]}]}}}}'`
leo: What's the expected cost delta? Rough guess: heuristics -> +6% GPU idle time, but avoids rescheduling churn which saved ~25% of lost work last hour.
nisha: I'll open PR to add a backpressure knob to warmpool attach (limit concurrent egress per node) — should be low-risk.
maya: Canary results in 8m: solver OOM events dropped from ~40/min to 1/min, pending GPU pods draining. Fragmentation metric (binpack fragmentation 90p) down ~12%.
cheng: Nice. Follow-up: schedule a proper solver-scaling change (increase memory cap) + longer term move some affinity rules to soft-affinity. Hard affinity for all tiny pods is the root cause.
sam: I'll keep the canary for 1h then roll to region. If any regressions, revert.
leo: Reassigning cost action item to finance for expected +6% burn if we keep heuristic long-term.
nisha: Noted — PR for attach-throttle in review.
maya: Closing the loop here — will post a short postmortem with timeline + config diff after we stabilize. :thumbsup:
